SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 3-day history of acute diarrhoea and vomiting.
  • Diarrhoea began watery, now “very loose”; ≥4 bowel motions today (exact count unclear).  
  • Associated cramp-like peri-umbilical abdominal pain that precedes urge to defecate.  
  • Persistent vomiting of all oral intake (including water, tea, ORS).  
  • Subjective fever (“literally boiling”); temperature not measured.  
  • No visible blood in stool or urine.  
  • Still passing urine; last void ~1 hour ago; colour not checked.  
  • No rash.

- Possible exposure: Brother with similar gastrointestinal illness; reported school outbreak. No recent travel.

- Past medical/surgical history: Denies chronic illnesses, prior abdominal problems, or surgeries.

- Medications:
  • Vitamin D daily (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • Occasional ibuprofen for dysmenorrhoea (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • Oral rehydration salts (homemade salt-sugar mix) 3×/day for 2 days.

- Social history:
  • Smoking: none.  
  • Alcohol: occasional pint.  
  • Recreational drugs: denies.  
  • Occupation: graphic designer; working from home today due to illness.  
  • Lives with mother and brother.

- Gynecologic: Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; not on contraception; not sexually active regularly.

- Allergies: Not discussed (information missing).

Objective:
- No physical examination performed (telephone consult).
- No vital signs available.
- No investigations completed yet.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhoea and vomiting
   - Assessment: Suspected infective gastroenteritis (likely viral; bacterial cause to be excluded).
   - Differential diagnosis: Bacterial gastroenteritis (e.g., Campylobacter, Salmonella, Shigella, E. coli); food-borne toxin; less likely inflammatory bowel disease flare (no history).
   - Investigations planned:
     • Stool sample for microscopy, culture & sensitivity.  
     • In-clinic hydration assessment (vitals, orthostatics, urinalysis) at urgent appointment.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Continue oral rehydration salts; small frequent sips.  
     • Bland diet (toast, biscuits); avoid dairy, fruit, vegetables until improving.  
     • Education on signs of dehydration and red-flag symptoms.  
   - Safety-net/Follow-up:
     • Urgent clinic appointment to submit stool sample and assess hydration.  
     • Advise emergency department attendance if worsening symptoms, inability to keep fluids down, reduced urine output, severe abdominal pain, or high fever.  
     • Patient to call support line to arrange appointment; clinician will facilitate booking.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Allergies not documented; no objective vitals; medication reconciliation limited to patient report.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor pauses but clinically adequate.
